narration: S07.1 Her check grew, but prices grew more, so today it buys less than her first check did.
S07.2 If her first check bought 10 crates of everything the index tracks, her check today buys about 9.
N1-s07-ruth.muted_read: "Back to the crate row: of 10 crates her first check bought, 9 stay lit today."

narration: S24.1 Ruth isn't the worst case, and she isn't the best.
S24.2 Carl, also illustrative, took the same kind of rising check in January 1966.
S24.3 His 20 years had the fastest price rise of any stretch: 6.38 percent a year.
S24.4 Like Ruth's, his first check bought a row of 10 crates.
S24.5 On every one of his 20 anniversaries, his check bought less than it had the year before.
S24.6 Ruth's check climbed back in her early years; Carl's never did.
N1-s24-carl.muted_read: "A second faceless figure over the 1966 tile with his row of 10 crates; a year counter ticks 1 to 20 and the row dims a little at every tick, never brightening, until about 4 are lit; a small inset of Ruth's line dipping and recovering early sits beside it."

narration: S27.1 Edna, also illustrative, started in January 1949, the last starting month when a 2 percent raise kept up.
S27.2 Twenty years later, her check still bought at least what her first one did.
S27.3 She is part of that early handful, and nobody who started after her got that answer.
S27.4 Her 20 years ended a few years into Carl's.
S27.5 The same few years of prices came at the end of her stretch, with all 10 crates still lit, and at the start of his.
N1-s27-edna.muted_read: "A third figure over the last `cushion` tile; her crate row ends fully lit. Her 20-year bar and Carl's on one time axis overlap at the end of hers / start of his; the shared years are shaded."

narration: S29.1 Same raise, same rule: Edna kept up, Ruth fell short late, and Carl fell far behind.
S29.2 In crates, Edna's row ended full, Ruth's at about 9, and Carl's at about 4.
S29.3 What differed was the month each one started, and what prices did after that.
N1-s29-three.muted_read: "Three figures side by side, each over a crate row: Edna all lit, Ruth 9 lit, Carl fewer than half; each labelled with a start month only."
